BAAHUBALI
 The Beginning (2015)    The Conclusion (2017)
An Indian epic action film franchise created by director S. S. Rajamouli, told across two parts. Set in
the mythical kingdom of Mahishmati, it weaves royal ambition, betrayal, love and revenge into one of
the most successful sagas in the history of Indian cinema. Made simultaneously in Telugu and Tamil
and dubbed into Hindi, Malayalam and other languages, the franchise became a nationwide

and dubbed into Hindi, Malayalam and other languages, the franchise became a nationwide
phenomenon - most famously for the cliffhanger question that gripped the country for two years:
"Why did Kattappa kill Baahubali?"

The Story
Part 1 - Baahubali: The Beginning (2015)
A woman flees a collapsing kingdom clutching an infant, escaping soldiers led by the cruel
commander. As she is swept away by a river, she raises the baby above the water with her last
strength before drowning. The child is rescued by a tribal community living at the foot of a colossal
waterfall and is raised as Shivudu.
Growing up, Shivudu is drawn by an irresistible pull to climb the towering waterfall. After many

Growing up, Shivudu is drawn by an irresistible pull to climb the towering waterfall. After many
attempts he finally scales it and discovers a world beyond - and a young warrior named Avanthika,
part of a rebel group fighting the tyrant king Bhallaladeva. Their mission is to free Devasena, a
queen who has been held in chains for twenty-five years. Shivudu takes up the cause, infiltrates the
capital of Mahishmati, and frees Devasena.

capital of Mahishmati, and frees Devasena.
In the ensuing battle Shivudu's true identity is revealed: he is Mahendra Baahubali, son of the
beloved late prince Amarendra Baahubali. The kingdom's old and loyal slave-warrior Kattappa
kneels before him. When Shivudu asks how his heroic father died, Kattappa delivers the film's
shattering final line - that it was he, Kattappa, who killed Baahubali.
Part 2 - Baahubali 2: The Conclusion (2017)

Part 2 - Baahubali 2: The Conclusion (2017)
The second film unfolds largely as a flashback that answers the question the nation was asking.
Years earlier, the wise queen mother Sivagami rules Mahishmati as regent and raises two cousins
as heirs: the noble, beloved Amarendra Baahubali and the ambitious, resentful Bhallaladeva. After
both prove themselves in a great battle against the invading Kalakeya horde, Sivagami names
Amarendra as the future king, while Bhallaladeva is made commander.

Amarendra as the future king, while Bhallaladeva is made commander.
Sent to tour the kingdom, Amarendra meets and falls in love with Devasena, the spirited princess of
Kuntala. Bhallaladeva, coveting both the throne and Devasena, manipulates his scheming father
Bijjaladeva and deceives Sivagami into promising Devasena to him. The misunderstanding spirals:
Amarendra chooses Devasena over blind obedience, is stripped of his position, and is eventually cast

out - yet remains adored by the common people.
Perceiving Amarendra as a threat to the crown, Bhallaladeva engineers a conspiracy and convinces
Sivagami that Amarendra means to seize power. Kattappa, bound by an unbreakable oath of loyalty
to the throne of Mahishmati, is ordered to act. Trapped between his love for Amarendra and his
sacred duty, Kattappa is forced to stab Baahubali in the back. Realising too late that she has been

sacred duty, Kattappa is forced to stab Baahubali in the back. Realising too late that she has been
deceived, a grief-stricken Sivagami declares Amarendra's infant son the true king before she is
betrayed - setting the stage for the child who will grow up to be Shivudu / Mahendra Baahubali.
In the present, Mahendra Baahubali rallies the people and the loyal Kattappa, storms Mahishmati,
and confronts Bhallaladeva in a final battle. He avenges his father, frees his mother Devasena, and

and confronts Bhallaladeva in a final battle. He avenges his father, frees his mother Devasena, and
reclaims the throne - restoring justice to the kingdom.

Principal Characters
Amarendra Baahubali - The noble, courageous and beloved prince of Mahishmati; a natural
leader chosen by Sivagami to be king. His integrity ultimately makes him a target.
Mahendra Baahubali (Shivudu) - Amarendra's son, raised in secret by tribal folk. He rediscovers
his heritage, avenges his father and reclaims the kingdom. (Same actor plays father and son.)
Bhallaladeva - Amarendra's envious cousin. Cunning and ruthless, he schemes his way to the

Bhallaladeva - Amarendra's envious cousin. Cunning and ruthless, he schemes his way to the
throne and rules as a tyrant - the saga's central antagonist.
Kattappa - The fiercely loyal slave-warrior sworn to serve the throne of Mahishmati across
generations. His forced killing of Baahubali is the emotional heart of the story.
Devasena - The proud, principled princess of Kuntala and Amarendra's wife; Mahendra's mother.
Imprisoned for 25 years, she never surrenders her dignity.

Imprisoned for 25 years, she never surrenders her dignity.
Rajamata Sivagami - The powerful queen mother and regent whose sense of duty and one fatal
misjudgement shape the kingdom's tragedy.
Bijjaladeva - Bhallaladeva's embittered, physically disabled father, denied the crown; the
poisonous voice behind his son's ambition.
Avanthika - A skilled warrior in the rebel resistance and Shivudu's love interest in the first film.

Kumara Varma - Devasena's cousin, a comic yet loyal figure whose pride is exploited in the
palace intrigue.

VFX
Multiple studios; landmark visual-effects work for Indian cinema
The two films were shot together over several years on enormous purpose-built sets, combining
practical construction with extensive visual effects to bring the kingdom of Mahishmati - its palaces,
waterfalls and battlefields - to life on an unprecedented scale for Indian cinema.

Music Album
The soundtrack and background score were composed by M. M. Keeravani. The music - sweeping,
choral and rooted in Indian classical and folk traditions - became integral to the epic's grandeur.
Telugu lyrics were largely penned by the composer and collaborators, with Hindi versions written by
Manoj Muntashir.

Reception, Records & Legacy
Baahubali: The Beginning (2015) was a massive critical and commercial success and won the
National Film Award for Best Feature Film, among other honours. Baahubali 2: The Conclusion
(2017) shattered box-office records to become the first Indian film to gross over Rs 1,000 crore
worldwide, with a global total widely reported above Rs 1,700 crore. Together the films earned

worldwide, with a global total widely reported above Rs 1,700 crore. Together the films earned
National Film Awards (including for special effects) and numerous South Indian and Filmfare awards.
Beyond the numbers, Baahubali reshaped expectations for Indian cinema - proving that a
regional-language epic could command a pan-India and global audience, and turning its cast, director
and the line "Why did Kattappa kill Baahubali?" into enduring pop-culture landmarks.

Themes & Symbols
Duty vs. love - Almost every tragedy in the saga flows from characters torn between personal
loyalty and sworn duty - above all Kattappa, and Sivagami.
Legitimate power - The story asks who deserves to rule: the one born to it, the one who seizes it,
or the one the people love.
The mother figure - Sivagami and Devasena anchor the epic; motherhood, sacrifice and
protection recur from the opening scene onward.

protection recur from the opening scene onward.
Fate and lineage - Shivudu's pull toward the waterfall symbolises destiny and the call of his true
heritage.
Trivia
  The cliffhanger "Why did Kattappa kill Baahubali?" became a national obsession and a viral
meme for the two years between the films.
  Both films were shot simultaneously in Telugu and Tamil, with the same scenes performed for
each version.

each version.
  The colossal Mahishmati sets and the waterfall were created through a mix of large practical
construction and extensive visual effects.
  Baahubali 2 opened to record-breaking collections and became the first Indian film to cross Rs
1,000 crore worldwide.
  The franchise expanded into novels, an animated series and other media exploring the world's
backstory.
